summary: Enabling Ansible pipelining is encouraged for z/OS since Python tags its pipes correctly and it is faster than file I/O. Set PYTHONSTDINENCODING to cp1047, or you may get a 'SyntaxError: Non-UTF-8 code' error.
questions: Should I enable pipelining for z/OS hosts?
What does SyntaxError Non-UTF-8 code starting with \x81 mean on z/OS?
What value should PYTHONSTDINENCODING have for z/OS?
Why is pipelining faster on z/OS?

answer_card.title: Enabling pipelining for z/OS hosts
answer_card.answer_md:
Enable `ANSIBLE_PIPELINING` in `ansible.cfg`. Module code is then sent through Python's stdin pipe in one call instead of via temp files. This is encouraged on z/OS because Python tags its pipes with the right encoding (fewer encoding errors) and pipes are faster than file I/O.

Also set this in the environment for z/OS tasks:

```yaml
PYTHONSTDINENCODING: "cp1047"
```

If pipelining is on but this isn't set correctly, you may see:

```text
SyntaxError: Non-UTF-8 code starting with '\x81' in file <stdin> on line 1, but no encoding declared
```
(the hex value may vary).
